correctness.rationale: The first image has coordinate upper bound exp(1/e)/n; the strict elementary bound exp(1+1/e)<4 puts it below 1/e for n>=4. Equal normalized images imply that all differences x log x - y log y are a common constant. Strict decrease on that branch would force a common strict coordinatewise inequality for a nonzero constant, impossible at equal sums. Iterating this injectivity back to time one proves the exact equivalence. In dimension three, the continuous scalar map takes 0 to sqrt(2)-1 and 1/3 to itself, so its image contains the entire interval between these points. Its log-odds derivative is g(s)=3/2+log(s)+(1/2)log((1-s)/2), strictly increasing on the interval, with g(1/3)<0 and g(sqrt(2)-1)>0 (e^3>20 and 10-7 sqrt(2)>1/10 by strict rational bounds). Each stated target has an antecedent on each side of the fold, both already in the first image, hence first equality at time two. The upper endpoint excludes the uniform target. Convergence does not obstruct exact merging: on the first image for n>=3 all coordinates are below 1/2, giving a bound M<1/2 for |x(1+log x)|, and thus contraction by at most 2M in the oscillation of log coordinate ratios. The independent diagnostic reproduces the exact rational comparisons and locates the fold at 0.4112527705787681; the interval proof is analytic.
residual_risks: The construction does not classify the remaining three-coordinate fibers, deeper merger times or mergers outside the symmetric line.
